taskId.description: The task to start the agent on, by the id list_tasks answered; with from, the task of the agent it starts from.

prompt.description: What the agent should do, typed to it as its first message; the developer's words where they named the job. Leave it out to start the agent on the task's description itself.

note.description: Everything else the agent should hear as it starts (what to start with, what to watch out for, what to leave alone), handed to it after the description or the prompt in the same first message; leave it out where there is nothing beyond the description.

title.description: The agent's title from the start, how the developer sees it named, such as the pull request it will open; leave it out to have it named from what it is told.

branch.description: The branch of the task's repository to clone the agent's checkout at and cut its own branch from, such as the repository's default branch or the head branch of a pull request it builds on; it must already be on GitHub. Required on a task with a repository, except with from; leave it out for a task with no repository or a start from another agent.

model.description: The model to run on, by its catalog id (such as anthropic/claude-opus-5.5); leave it out with the effort for the member's default.

effort.description: The reasoning effort, as the model lists it (such as high); given with the model or not at all.

runsOn.description: Where the agent runs: {"machine":"vercel"} for the cloud, or {"machine":"device","device":"<name>"} for one of the member's own devices (a Mac or a host) by its name, or {"machine":"device","deviceId":"<id>"} by its id; it must be online, and a name matching none of their devices, or several, is refused with the devices listed. list_machines lists each place with the runsOn to pass. Every start names it but one with from, which runs where the agent it starts from runs unless it names another place, which moves it there.

agentId.description: The agent to start from, by the id list_agents answered.

messageId.description: One of that agent's messages, by the messageId read_agent names on an entry of its transcript, to fork it there; leave it out to continue the agent from where it stands.

from.description: Another agent of your workspace to take over from, on its own task: the new agent is handed its brief, its transcript (with Vespin's summary of the steps that do not fit), and a copy of its work, runs on its model unless you name one, and hears the note after them; it takes no prompt and no branch. Without messageId it continues the agent, which is stopped; with one it forks the agent at that message, which goes on.
